page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.large is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, which correspond to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes an L3 cache of 480 MB, alongside 48 KB of L1d cache and 2 MB of L2 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage, bundled GPUs, or baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2056.0 and strong single-threaded compression performance, achieving 33.85 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.22 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is poor at 2147.27, and the Passmark memory score is also poor at 1238.89. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths are restricted to 19.96 GB/sec and 14.37 GB/sec respectively, both falling into the bottom 10% tier.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the m8i-flex.large is suited for workloads that rely on single-threaded CPU performance rather than high memory throughput or parallelized multi-core execution. It is appropriate for basic text processing, light web serving, and small-scale language model inference, where it achieves 102.36 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model. The instance offers an entry-level general-purpose resource profile, trading off multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth for single-core efficiency.
